title: CASAN criteria catalogue
description: The rubric behind every H1..H7 evidence score (portal/backend/config/casan-criteria.yaml). It is the ONE file that decides what a project is scored on, so it is schema-validated like every other policy file (C8): a typo in `check` silently turned a machine control into something an admin could self-attest, and a missing `why` leaves a criterion nobody can argue with.

source_doc.description: Where the criteria come from. Every criterion's `source` points into this document, which is what makes a score traceable rather than asserted.

attestation_ttl_days.description: How long a human attestation counts as evidence; 0 disables expiry. A claim with no machine proof ages out like any other evidence (harness convention, not a requirement of source_doc).

rubric_dimensions.description: Judge-rubric dimensions a prompt_score row must ALL carry before H3-2 counts it. Must match app/models/prompt_score.py.

ledger_verify_entries.description: How many most-recent ledger entries H5-2 recomputes entry_hash for.

action_path.description: Dotted path to the list of classified actions in risk-registry.yaml — the thing H5-3 actually asks for.

tier_path.description: Dotted path to the severity tiers; reported for context, not required for the verdict.

registry_thresholds.description: H2 scoring thresholds. They were literals inside the check functions while every other tunable came from this file, so an operator could not see — let alone change — what 'registry đủ lớn' meant (C2).

min_entries.description: H2-2: a tool registry with fewer entries than this is a stub, not a registry.

contract_coverage_pct.description: H2-1: percent of registry entries that must declare both input and output contracts.

idempotency_coverage_pct.description: H2-3: percent of side-effect tools that must declare an idempotency_key_pattern.

context_ttl_default_minutes.description: H1-2 freshness TTL used only when the project's own casan-policies declares no context.staleness_ttl_minutes.

alert_threshold_paths.description: H6-3: the dotted paths in the project's casan-policies that app/core/alerts.py actually reads. Each must be present and NON-ZERO. Matching key *names* instead passed `agentops: {alert_bananas: {quantity: 7}}` and a threshold of 0, while alerts.py ran on its built-in defaults.

drift_threshold_paths.description: H6-4: the dotted paths app/core/alerts.py:check_drift() consumes. Present and non-zero, or drift detection is not configured.

drift_disable_paths.description: H6-4: paths whose false/off value means the project declared drift detection OFF. `any key containing "drift"` scored a DISABLED config as configured.

drift_scripts.description: H6-4: client-side drift scripts; any one present satisfies the script half (PowerShell primary, bash parity — C7).

snapshot_retention_per_project.description: How many pushed evidence snapshots app/api/ingest.py keeps per project; only the newest is ever read. 0 disables pruning.

doctor_report_retention_per_project.description: How many pushed `harness doctor` reports app/api/ingest.py keeps per project. Unlike the CASAN snapshot, doctor is recomputed and pushed on every sync, so without a cap a frequently-synced project accumulates rows forever. 0 disables pruning.

snapshot_retention_per_checkout.description: How many pushed evidence snapshots app/api/ingest.py keeps per (project, checkout) group; the group of rows with no checkout is its own group. Wins over snapshot_retention_per_project when both are set. 0 disables pruning.

doctor_report_retention_per_checkout.description: How many pushed `harness doctor` reports app/api/ingest.py keeps per (project, checkout) group; the group of rows with no checkout is its own group. Wins over doctor_report_retention_per_project when both are set. 0 disables pruning.

workflow_min_stages.description: Minimum stages before H7-1 will look for a dependency edge. Below 2 a DAG cannot have one.

script.description: Marker that must appear in the hook command or its args for the hook to count as wired.

closing_question.description: The one question the layer exists to answer, quoted from source_doc.

allOf.description: Every machine-checked criterion must say where its evidence comes from. Without it the evaluator has to guess, and the guess that blanked out the four telemetry-only criteria told the whole fleet 'chưa đo được' about rows in the Portal's own database.

source.description: Where in source_doc this criterion is stated.

why.description: Why it matters. Required: a criterion nobody can justify is a criterion nobody will fix.

weight.description: Relative weight in the layer score. Omitted = 1.

check.description: Name of the automatic check in casan_criteria.CHECKS. null (`check: ~`) means the machine cannot prove it — ONLY those criteria are attestable by a human, because an attestation that could overturn a check the machine ran turns the evidence axis into an opinion.

data_source.description: Where the check reads its evidence. `telemetry` = the Portal's own tables only, so it runs whether or not the server can see the project's files. `repo` = the project's governance files. `mixed` = both, and it is unmeasured without the files. A repo/mixed criterion with no file source — or whose file the dev machine deliberately withheld — is UNMEASURED: excluded from both sides of the score fraction, never counted as a failure.
